title: Coastline Systems — Migration walkthrough to Redwood API
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran a migration-focused demo for Coastline Systems to map current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to Redwood API semantics. Discussed model parity, tokenization differences, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/private deployment requirements, and an initial POC plan. Action items include sending mapping sheet, security pack, and scheduling a 2-week pilot baseline run with quantized models.

transcript:
Meeting header: April 10, 2026 15:00 PT — Duration: 49 mins — Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM) — Ava (Coastline CTO), Rohit (Sr ML Eng), Liam (DevOps), Priya (Product)

Summary: Jordan opened with context, Maya walked through live API examples and the Console, Samir covered billing/next-steps, and the team drilled into latency, caching, and private deployment considerations. Transcript may contain mis-transcriptions and speaker attribution noise.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood, this is Maya on the SE side and Samir from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Ava: Good, thanks. We've been wanting to go through the migration plan; we currently have endpoints on OpenAI and Anthropic and a few services on Together, and we want to consolidate.
[00:18] Jordan: Great, that's the goal for today — show the mapping, the console controls, and an Optimize quick-pass to show cost fixes. Roughly 45 minutes, leave 10 at end for Qs.
[00:28] Rohit: Quick note — we have strict residency rules for certain datasets, and we also need KMS integration.
[00:33] Samir: Noted, we'll show the Private options and KMS notes.
[00:38] Maya: I'll start with a small demo — code-first mapping of a Together/TogetherAI chat endpoint to Redwood's chat API. We'll also show a generator path for OpenAI-style completions.
[00:47] [00:47] Maya: (screen share) Ok, here's an existing OpenAI snippet — their call looks like openai.ChatCompletion.create with messages array and stop token. With Redwood the same payload maps to POST /v1/chat/completions but couple of parameter names differ, for example Redwood uses model_selector and route tags — sorry, bad word — but essentially you can keep messages and role.
[01:12] Rohit: Are there differences in tokenization that could affect pricing? We use byte-pair tokenization and some of our prompts hit edge cases.
[01:20] Maya: Good q; model families differ, and tokenization can vary a few percent. We include a parity mapping sheet that rewrites prompt boundaries and shows token delta estimates. For your samples we can run a tokenizer comparison.
[01:35] Ava: We'd want to know worst-case cost delta, not just averages.
[01:38] Jordan: We'll run the samples in the pilot and include cost per 1M tokens for both baseline and Redwood quantized options.
[01:45] [01:45] Maya: Now here is a Together endpoint — they use stream websockets for lower latency. Redwood supports streaming over chunked HTTP and websockets; the SDKs will be nearly identical. Example: streaming events come back with token fragments and finish event. If you rely on the 'role' fields, those map 1:1.
[02:08] Liam: Our infra team is worried about connection churn — will the client libraries handle auto-reconnect?
[02:12] Maya: Yes, we have SDKs with reconnect logic and backoff; if you're using our hosted API you get connection pooling at the edge. For Dedicated and Private, your infra team can put their own LB.
[02:23] Rohit: About model variants — we use a small 13B for most completion traffic and a 70B for heavy tasks. Can we pin versions?
[02:31] Jordan: Absolutely. You can pin and also do traffic splitting in the Console — canary or percentage rollouts. Maya will show Rollouts in a sec.
[02:39] [02:39] Maya: Console demo — here's the Model Catalog, you can see recommended latency profiles and quant options. I click into a model and see perf profiles: 13B int8 is our recommended for high throughput; 70B int8 int4 variants for higher quality. There's a toggle for 'dedicated' vs 'hosted'.
[02:59] Rohit: How transparent are the cost numbers in the Console? We need token-level drilldown per route.
[03:05] Maya: We show per-route token counts, per-model CPU/GPU time, and estimated cost. For Dedicated we show allocation and per-pod utilization. You can export CSVs for finance.
[03:18] [03:18] Ava: Security — we need SSO (SAML), audit logs, and HSM-backed KMS. Are those available for Private?
[03:25] Samir: Yes, Private ships with SAML SSO integrations, RBAC, and audit logs. KMS can be customer-managed via external HSM or cloud provider KMS (we have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). We'll send the SOC2 pack.
[03:41] Rohit: Any gotchas on provenance of logs? We can't have PII in logs for certain flows.
[03:48] Samir: We support redaction and field-level masking at the ingestion layer and can configure log retention policies per customer.
[03:56] [03:56] Jordan: Back to parity — here's the mapping sheet (live) — column A original endpoint, column B Redwood equivalent, column C changes: stop_token -> stop_sequences, presence_penalty -> penalty.presence, etc. Note: some provider-specific features like Together's 'persona profile' map to Redwood metadata which you can attach to requests and enforce in runtime hooks.
[04:18] Rohit: Ok, show us an example of a prompt where tokenization changed cost significantly.
[04:22] Maya: (switches tabs) For one of your invoice parsers, the tokenizer splits a long hyphenated ID differently; delta was ~6% tokens. We show a rewrite that uses pre-tokenized embeddings and a cache to reduce repeated context.
[04:36] [04:36] Jordan: That ties into Optimize — our Optimize engine will recommend prefix caching for templates that repeat across calls, saving you tokens and latency. Maya: can you show the Optimize suggestion UI?
[04:45] Maya: Sure — here's Optimize recommendations: batching window 25ms for your throughput pattern, prefix cache for the invoice template, and quantization suggestion int8 for 13B. It also shows expected cost reduction (roughly 22% for token-heavy flows).
[04:58] Priya: How invasive are code changes to enable prefix caching?
[05:02] Maya: Minimal — attach a cache key to the request metadata; we provide helper functions in SDK to compute keys from prompt templates. No model changes required.
[05:09] [05:09] Rohit: Latency numbers — what's the p95 for 13B int8 on hosted vs dedicated?
[05:14] Maya: Hosted p95 is ~180-250ms depending on seq len; Dedicated can push to 80-120ms with batching and pre-allocated KV cache. We'll include benchmark runs in the POC.
[05:25] Liam: For our use case we care about 100ms SLO for interactive features. That seems tight on hosted.
[05:30] Jordan: For sub-100ms we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with pre-warmed pools and optimized kernels. We'll run a micro-benchmark.
[05:38] [05:38] Ava: Can we do a quick demo of a full migration path — SDK code sample, a Console deploy, and a traffic shift to 10%?
[05:44] Maya: Yes. (screen share) SDK snippet: current OpenAI: client.create({model, messages}) — Redwood: import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference' and use client.chat.create({model: 'rwd-13b', messages, route: 'coastline-prod'}). Then in Console I create a route, attach model, and click 'Deploy'.
[06:08] Jordan: Now I'll show traffic shifting — create a rollout, set 90% to legacy endpoint (we proxy) and 10% to Redwood; observe metrics. (pauses) You can see latency and error metrics for both groups.
[06:30] Rohit: Proxying sounds good for gradual migration — does Redwood proxy calls back to OpenAI if a feature isn't supported?
[06:36] Maya: We have compatibility routing; you can set fallback to upstream providers for specific endpoints. That's nice for features not yet ported.
[06:44] [06:44] Ava: What about hallucination differences when moving models — our QA shows different behaviors across vendors.
[06:49] Maya: We include eval harnesses and regression alerts — you can attach prompts sets and the system tracks divergence in output distributions and flags regressions. You can set auto-fallback if quality drops beyond threshold.
[07:05] Rohit: For the pilot, can we run side-by-side A/B with real traffic for two weeks and capture quality metrics?
[07:10] Jordan: Absolutely — typical POC is 2 weeks side-by-side with sample traffic and dedicated evals. We'll define baseline metrics: latency p95, tokens per request, accuracy on labeled prompt set, and cost per 1M tokens.
[07:23] [07:23] Maya: Now I'll show a snippet of the Console's Optimize tab — it suggests quantization tradeoffs with estimated quality delta. You can accept a suggestion to create a new model variant and roll it to a small percentage.
[07:35] Liam: For Dedicated how do upgrades work? Does model change require downtime?
[07:40] Maya: No, rollouts are zero-downtime — traffic shifting between model variants. For infra changes we have canary provisioning to avoid service disruption.
[07:50] [07:50] Rohit: Any edge cases for streaming token-level stops and function calls? We're heavy on structured output and function-calling.
[07:57] Maya: Function calling maps to Redwood's tooling — you define function spec, we return structured JSON; streaming includes tool-call events. For complex nested tool calls there are minor syntax differences but we provide a compat layer in SDK. We'll include code samples.
[08:14] Jordan: Security specifics — Samir?
[08:17] Samir: For Private deployments we deploy a control plane in a customer VPC; data plane can be customer-hosted. Audit logs ship to your SIEM via syslog or S3. KMS integrations provide envelope encryption; keys never leave your HSM.
[08:31] Ava: Does Redwood retain any prompts or outputs for hosted customers? We need data retention guarantees.
[08:36] Samir: Hosted defaults to ephemeral logs for L3 customers; for enterprise we can set no retention or encrypt logs with customer KMS and set retention windows. We'll share the redaction and retention config doc.
[08:48] [08:48] Rohit: How is billing handled during a POC? We prefer not to be charged for test runs beyond a small pilot fee.
[08:53] Jordan: We usually provide trial credits for POC plus a short-term billable pilot if you want dedicated capacity. We'll outline options in the follow-up.
[08:59] Maya: Quick note about embeddings — if you plan to migrate retrievers, embedding vector format is compatible; we support cosine/l2 and have migration tools for index export/import.
[09:10] Priya: We use a hybrid retrieval + generative flow — would Redwood Optimize recommend different model per route?
[09:16] Maya: Yes, Optimize will recommend cheapest model that meets quality targets per route; it can also suggest using sparse cache for common doc lookups.
[09:26] [09:26] Jordan: Let's jump to an example of an SDK diff for a real endpoint. (shares code) Old: openai.Completion.create({engine:'davinci', prompt}) — New: redwood.completions.create({model:'rwd-13b-int8', prompt, meta: {route: 'invoice-parser'}})
[09:46] Rohit: Any additional libraries or middleware? We currently use an internal wrapper.
[09:50] Maya: Your wrapper will mostly be unchanged; the client instantiation changes and a few param names. We can help with a migration script.
[09:58] [09:58] Ava: Ok, let's talk timelines — we want a production cut in Q3. Is that realistic?
[10:03] Jordan: Yes — a typical timeline: 2-week POC, 4-6 week integration and testing, then staged rollout. Q3 is reasonable.
[10:13] Liam: One more ops question — how are model updates audited? We need a changelog + approval flow.
[10:18] Maya: The Console has an audit trail and an approvals workflow for model deployments; you can require an approver before traffic shift.
[10:26] [10:26] Rohit: Anything else on infra? Our security team will ask about IP allowlists and private endpoints.
[10:31] Samir: Private supports IP allowlists and private endpoints over VPC peering. We'll prepare a network diagram in the security pack.
[10:39] Jordan: I'll summarize next steps — Jordan to share parity sheet and SDK diffs, Maya to draft POC runbook, Samir to share SOC2 + network diagrams, Coastline to provide sample prompts. Any objections?
[10:50] Ava: Sounds good, please include estimated costs for hosted vs dedicated for our baseline traffic.
[10:55] Jordan: Will do.
[11:00] [11:00] Rohit: Great. Two small clarifications — can the fallback routing be set per-route and per-tenant?
[11:06] Maya: Yes, per-route, and you can scope to tenants via metadata.
[11:10] Priya: Also, can we run small synthetic benchmarks inside our environment?
[11:14] Maya: We'll provide a bench harness you can run and we can run a corresponding job on Redwood side for comparison.
[11:20] Jordan: Ok we'll follow up with links and schedule the POC kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[11:25] Ava: Thanks.
[11:27] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label noise (timestamps are approximated). The transcript includes paraphrases and condensed segments for brevity.
